sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Microservices interview questions test architectural judgement, not just framework knowledge — service decomposition, API gateway patterns, service discovery, client- vs server-side load balancing, circuit breaker / retry / bulkhead / time limiter (Resilience4j), saga and outbox patterns, distributed tracing (correlation IDs, OpenTelemetry, Zipkin), config management (Spring Cloud Config), service mesh (sidecars, Istio basics), and the migration patterns from monolith to microservices (strangler fig). Pair this with the REST API and Messaging/Kafka pages for the full microservices interview surface.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Microservices = **independent deployability + bounded contexts**, paid for in operational complexity.

- **Service boundary** = bounded context (DDD); never split by tech layer.
- **Sync** (REST / gRPC) vs **Async** (Kafka / SNS) — pick by coupling tolerance.
- **Resilience** — retry, circuit-breaker, bulkhead, timeout (Resilience4j).
- **Discovery** — server-side (LB) vs client-side (Eureka).
- **Tracing** — OpenTelemetry; correlation IDs are non-negotiable.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **Distributed transactions** — don't; use saga (orchestration vs choreography) and outbox.
- **Strangler-fig** — the only sane monolith → microservices migration pattern.
- **Service mesh** — sidecars (Istio / Linkerd) move resilience out of code, at infra cost.
- **Contract testing** — Pact / Spring Cloud Contract — prevents the cross-service break.
- **Cost** — every new service is a new pager; senior answer always weighs ops cost.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"I'd start with a modular monolith, split out the service when <coupling pain / scale boundary> appears, communicate sync via <REST | gRPC> and async via <Kafka> with the outbox pattern, wrap calls in Resilience4j circuit-breakers, and stand up tracing on day one."*
